accepted.evidence: Turner 9383 directly gives European Romani phen- 'to speak' under bhánati. The source prints phen-ipej 'to say; to tell' and defines productive infinitive -ipej after the present stem (p. 142 §3.17.3.1); the suffix is not a separate historical root. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner 9416 gives Greek/Hungarian Romani uv-/ov- 'become, is' under bhávati. The source prints oj-ipey 'to become' as the copular subjunctive/imperfect stem (p. 142 §3.18.2); its §2.3.13 describes Zargari present-stem v > j, supporting the local oj- form. The productive infinitive is retained. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner 4008 §1 explicitly gives European Romani gelo as the past of 'go'. The source lists irregular gender/first-person forms gölu 'he went', geli 'she went', gölum 'I went' (p. 140 §3.10.2). These are ordinary inflections of its inherited perfect stem, preserving ö/e alternation and person/gender endings. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.
